summary: Post-audit fix regression for IMORA Tchad — SEC-001 (CORS), SEC-002 (media caps create+update), SEC-003 (legacy /auth/session gated), report rate-limit hardening, email_verified default. 27/28 pass (+ 1 xfail documenting an internal bug in document size cap). Prior suites (test_security_fixes, test_hardening) also re-run: 66/68 pass — the 2 residual failures are a pre-existing rate-limiter design gap around ingress IP handling (see below) and one collateral test starvation in test_hardening.

minor.issue: BUG in _validate_property_media (server.py:778-780): iterates `for doc in payload.documents` where documents is List[dict]. `len(doc)` returns the number of keys in the dict (always 3: type/name/data), NOT the byte size of the base64 payload. Consequence: oversize document cap (_MAX_DOCUMENT_BYTES=8MB) is never enforced. Fix: change to `len(doc.get('data', ''))` (mirroring the photo/video check). Test test_document_too_large_413 currently marked xfail to record the regression.

Rate-limit key uses `request.client.host` which behind Cloudflare/ingress resolves to the ingress pod IP (observed 2 rotating IPs: 10.208.128.2/6). A single attacker's burst is therefore de-facto capped at (6 × number-of-ingress-hops), not 6/min. Preview run: 12 accepted, 3 rejected out of 15. Authenticated path (per-user-id) works correctly. Fix: honor X-Forwarded-For (first hop) OR configure app.middleware to set request.client from XFF, then continue using .host.

action_items: Fix document byte-size cap: replace `len(doc)` with `len(doc.get('data', ''))` in _validate_property_media on both create and update paths (server.py:778-780).
Fix anonymous report rate-limit to use X-Forwarded-For (client real IP) instead of ingress IP; otherwise cap is effectively multiplied by ingress fan-out.

(Optional) Add pytest.fixture(scope='session') sleeps or dedicated test rate-limit reset to avoid collateral 429s between rate-limit tests and other tests using the same identity (test_hardening.test_report_authenticated_ok failed only when audited in the same session).
critical_code_review_comments: SEC-002: documents cap uses `len(dict)` — silently bypassable. Photos/videos use `len(str)` correctly.

SEC-001: CORS fix verified — untrusted / evil / arbitrary preview subdomains no longer reflected. Trusted origins (imoratchad.com, preview URL) still allowed at the FastAPI layer. Cloudflare edge still may inject `*` per prior test_hardening SEC003 notes; that's a platform-layer concern.
SEC-003: /api/auth/session returns 410 by default (ENABLE_LEGACY_EMERGENT_AUTH gates it). Verified.

email_verified default: /auth/google callback rejects any userinfo where email_verified is falsy/missing (`info.get('email_verified', False)`). Verified statically. Note: User model in /app/backend/server.py still defaults `email_verified: bool = True` at model level (verified absence via grep). If persisted users are consulted for verified state later, keep this in sync.
server.py is 1678 lines — split into routers already recommended in iter 3, still pending.
Report rate limiter reuses AI helper (6/min sliding window) — good, but per-IP behind CDN is weak (see minor issue above).

success_rate.backend: 96% (27/28 including one xfail documenting a real bug)

seed_data_creation: Multiple TEST_-prefixed reports created during rate-limit bursts (per anon/auth test); one property created+deleted in CRUD flow; owned_property module fixture cleaned up on teardown.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run `pytest /app/backend/tests/test_audit_fixes.py -v` (~80s). Video-oversize tests hit http://localhost:8001 directly to bypass Cloudflare 413. If document size cap is fixed by main agent, flip xfail → strict pass. Beware rate-limit tests consume the 6/min window for the authenticated PART user — space 65s between rate-limit and normal report tests, or split runs.
rca of the issue: Two real bugs surfaced by these tests: (1) documents oversize check is a no-op due to len() on a dict — trivial one-line fix. (2) Anonymous report rate limit uses request.client.host which behind a load-balanced ingress = ingress IP, not user IP; effective cap scales with ingress hop count. Both are backend-only, no infrastructure changes required.
